summary: Add PostgreSQL to a Next.js or SvelteKit app through Drizzle, with SQL migrations and isolated database tests.
description: Add PostgreSQL to Next.js or SvelteKit through Drizzle ORM and the pg driver: Docker Compose services for development and tests, checked-in SQL migrations with a drift check, a server-only database module, one repository behind the starter items service and a readiness route. Each test file gets its own database cloned from a migrated template, and the end-to-end run gets its own too. Your product tables, queries and access rules are still to write; hosting a production database is separate.
seoDescription: Postgres for Next.js and SvelteKit through Drizzle ORM and pg, with checked-in SQL migrations and isolated database tests.

projectExamples.title: Team request tracker
projectExamples.description: Store requests and their status in Postgres through Drizzle repositories behind Server Actions. Add sign-in and per-team access rules before sharing it.

projectExamples.title: Inventory catalog with history
projectExamples.description: Keep catalog items and change records in your own tables, with migrations reviewed in pull requests and each test file on a private database.

plain.whatItIs: Adds a PostgreSQL database server to a Next.js or SvelteKit app, with Drizzle for queries and saved steps for table changes.
goodAt: Running a local database on your own computer for development and tests
Giving each test file its own copy of the database, made from a ready template
Saving table changes as steps, and checking them against the code's schema
notGoodAt: Hosting a live production database; arrange a hosting provider separately.
Other stacks; the Effect and FastAPI Postgres add-ons are built for those.
